settings.content: Ink on paper. All color in the store comes from photography — there is no accent color in the UI.

settings.label: Secondary label
settings.info: Used for secondary text everywhere. The default clears WCAG AA (4.5:1) on both paper and cream — 5.14:1 and 4.67:1. Lightening it past roughly #767168 drops below AA on paper.

settings.label: Buy bar color
settings.info: Amber is the ONLY place a warm tone may appear. Checkout Pay button follows at go-live (manual checkout editor).

settings.label: Amber (buy bar only)
settings.info: Used only when the buy bar is set to Amber. Never a UI accent.

settings.content: The buy bar picks its own label colour: the theme measures the contrast of your amber against both ink and paper and prints whichever wins. The shipped amber gives 3.19:1 with paper (below the 4.5:1 minimum for the bar's 14px label) and 5.48:1 with ink, so it is labelled in ink. Pick a darker amber and the label flips back to paper on its own — you cannot land on an illegible buy bar from this field.
Surface tones. These two are structural, not decorative: they give the page a chapter rhythm and a second voice for prose, which is the difference between a long page and a long scroll.

settings.label: Limestone (alternating section band)
settings.info: Backs every other section so the page reads as chapters instead of one flat sheet. Deliberately only 1.08:1 against paper — a band you notice at arm's length and not up close. Ink holds 16.2:1 on it and the secondary label 4.75:1, so no text needs re-checking. Going darker than roughly #EDE9E0 stops reading as the same paper and starts reading as a coloured block.

settings.label: Ink soft (secondary prose)
settings.info: For running prose that is not the primary voice — descriptions, captions, editorial body. Distinct from the Secondary label above: this is for sentences, that is for 14px uppercase chrome. The default holds 8.75:1 on paper, 8.08:1 on limestone and 7.96:1 on cream, so it clears WCAG AAA (7:1) on all three grounds and stays a real prose colour rather than grey filler.

settings.content: The theme ships Prata (display) and Archivo (everything else) as its own font files, preloaded before the stylesheet is even parsed. LEAVE BOTH PICKERS ALONE and those local files keep being used — the store makes no request to Shopify's font service at all, which is the fastest of the two paths. Pick any other family and that role moves over to Shopify's fonts, costing one extra connection on first paint. Both are correct; the default is faster.

settings.label: Display font
settings.info: Headlines only: hero, section headings, editorial captions, product title, and the short italic tags under the product name. NOTE: Prata is no longer offered in Shopify's font list, so this picker sits on DM Serif Display — the nearest match — to mean "the theme's own Prata". At that setting your headlines render in Prata. Change it to anything else and you get exactly the family you picked. The one quirk: choosing DM Serif Display on purpose also gives you Prata. A high-contrast serif is what makes this store read as editorial rather than as a storefront — if you swap it, swap it for another serif.

settings.label: Body + interface font
settings.info: Everything else: the uppercase label system, buttons, navigation, prices and body copy. Left on Archivo this uses the theme's own file. A grotesque with a true italic and a real bold works best — the theme asks for regular, bold and italic cuts, and a single-weight family will have its bold synthesised by the browser.

settings.label: Type scale
settings.info: Scales every display step together (-8% / +8%), so the relationship between the hero, section headings and captions is preserved — it moves the whole scale, it does not resize one heading. Generous suits short catalogues with big photography; Compact suits dense category pages.

settings.label: Heading letter-spacing
settings.info: In hundredths of an em. -0.5 is the -0.005em the display steps ship with. Serif display faces need negative tracking at hero size (96px) and roughly none at caption size; if you have chosen a geometric or condensed display font, opening this up to 0 or 0.5 is usually the fix. Past 1 the word shapes come apart at hero size.

settings.label: Body text size
settings.info: 17px is the shipped default and is deliberately one step above the usual 16: the theme's readership skews older, and larger body type costs a younger reader nothing. Drop to 15 only if you have chosen a body font that runs wide.

settings.content: These three settings control the page's structure: how wide it gets, how much air sits between sections, and whether corners are sharp. They are the settings that make one store look like a different store.

settings.label: Page width
settings.info: The maximum width of contained content. Full-bleed rows (hero, category mosaic) ignore it by design. Wider is not better: past about 1400 a four-up product row starts showing cards larger than the photography was shot for.

settings.label: Section spacing
settings.info: Sets the whole spacing system at once — page gutters, the gaps inside grids, and the space between sections — as one proportional set, so nothing has to be nudged individually. Every value scales with the viewport, so Airy does not mean an empty phone screen.

settings.label: Corners
settings.info: Sharp is the theme's signal — square corners are what a serif display face and a hairline rule system are built around, and it is why the store reads as print rather than as an app. Soft and Round are here because a preset may want them; they apply to cards and media, never to the uppercase label chrome.

settings.content: The product card appears on the homepage, every collection, search, the cart cross-sell and the related row — it is the most-repeated object in the store, so these settings change more of it than anything else here.

settings.label: Image shape
settings.info: Every card is cropped to the same shape so a grid reads as a grid — mixed source ratios are the single biggest thing that makes a catalogue look unfinished. Choose the one closest to how your photography was actually shot: cropping a square packshot to 2:3 cuts the garment.

settings.label: Hover behaviour
settings.info: Second image cross-fades to the product's second photo and falls back to no effect on products that only have one — it is the most useful of the three because it answers "what does the back look like" without a click. Zoom is the safe choice for a catalogue with inconsistent second shots. None is correct on touch-only storefronts.

settings.label: Show vendor on cards
settings.info: Off by default: in a single-brand store the vendor is the same word under every card, which adds a line of type and no information. Turn it on for a multi-brand or stockist catalogue, where it is the first thing a shopper scans for.

settings.label: Quick add on cards
settings.info: Adds a one-tap add control to the card. For a product with sizes it opens the size choice rather than guessing a variant — a quick-add that silently picks a size is a returns problem.

settings.label: Show cents in prices
settings.info: Drives EVERY price in the theme — cards, product page, cart, drawer, totals — so the store cannot print $240.00 in one place and $240 in another. Off shows whole amounts where the price has no cents and keeps them where it does (so $19.99 is never truncated). On always shows two decimals, which is the right choice for a market that expects them.

settings.content: Your store's name comes from Shopify (Settings → Store details) and is used automatically. These two fields only add what Shopify cannot know: how you describe yourself.

settings.label: Homepage tagline
settings.info: Appended to your store name in the browser tab and in link previews, e.g. "Store name – Everyday knitwear". Leave empty to show the store name alone. Do not name a product category you do not sell.

settings.label: Homepage meta description
settings.info: The search-result snippet for your homepage, ~155 characters. Empty = no description tag, which lets Google pick its own text. Never promise shipping or returns terms you do not honour.

settings.label: Logo
settings.info: Shown in the header, footer and password page. Empty = your store name is set in type instead.

settings.label: Square logo (structured data)
settings.info: Square, at least 112px — Google reads this for the seller logo in Shopping results and the knowledge panel. Empty = the logo is omitted from structured data rather than pointing at a missing file.

settings.label: VAT ID
settings.info: Printed in the footer seller block. Empty = line hidden.

settings.label: Returns note (footer)
settings.info: Empty = line hidden.

settings.label: Free shipping line
settings.info: Back it with a $0 rate in your delivery profiles.

settings.label: GA4 Measurement ID
settings.info: Leave blank to disable. Example: G-XXXXXXXXXX

settings.label: Google Ads Conversion ID
settings.info: Example: AW-XXXXXXXXX

settings.content: Cart add-ons. Each must be an UNLISTED product with 'requires shipping' off, published to the Online Store only — never to Google & YouTube, or it enters the Shopping feed as a product.

settings.label: Cart add-on 1 (product handle)
settings.info: e.g. shipping-protection. A handle, not a picker: unlisted products are invisible to a product picker in Liquid. Empty = row hidden.

settings.label: Cart add-on 2 (product handle)
settings.info: e.g. priority-shipping. Empty = row hidden.

settings.content: Add-ons must not be pre-selected by default: a pre-ticked paid add-on is an additional payment under Art. 22 Consumer Rights Directive 2011/83/EU and requires the shopper's express opt-in before checkout — pre-selection may only be enabled for markets where it is lawful. Each add-on must stay a clearly labelled, separately priced cart line the shopper can add in one click — that is what keeps an opt-in add-on from being a hidden fee.

settings.label: Pre-select cart add-ons
settings.info: A pre-ticked paid add-on is not valid consent for an additional payment under Art. 22 Consumer Rights Directive 2011/83/EU, and carries similar risk under other consumer-protection regimes (e.g. FTC). Adds both add-ons the first time a real product enters the bag, if turned on; a shopper who unticks or removes one is never asked again in that session. Both stay visible, priced and removable above the total — keep it that way, a hidden pre-ticked paid add-on is a chargeback and compliance risk.

settings.label: Cart reservation countdown (minutes)
settings.info: 0 = no countdown. Nothing is actually reserved (inventory is untracked). A fabricated reservation countdown is a fake-urgency dark pattern under consumer-protection law in many jurisdictions, the same class as the id-modulo scarcity line. Re-enable only if the countdown is backed by genuine inventory-hold logic.

settings.content: ⚠️ Rating shown above the product title and under the checkout button. Both fields ship EMPTY and must stay empty until you have a real review base to quote: enter only numbers you can evidence from your own orders. Publishing a rating you cannot substantiate breaches consumer-protection law (DSA Art. 25, FTC fake-review rule) and Google's structured-data policy. The theme never links to or scrapes an external review profile.

settings.label: Rating value
settings.info: Printed as-is next to the stars, e.g. "4.7". Empty = the whole rating row is hidden everywhere.

settings.label: Review count
settings.info: Printed as-is, e.g. "1,284". Empty = only the value shows.

settings.content: Urgency + social-proof lines. These are NOT read from live inventory (inventory is untracked, policy CONTINUE) — they are fixed copy by design. Empty = the line does not render.

settings.label: Low-stock line
settings.default: Almost sold out, only a few left in stock

settings.label: Stack & save line
settings.default: Stack & save — buy more, get a bigger discount

settings.content: Trust box under the add button, and the ✔ promise lines. Enter only facts your store actually honours — a returns window or guarantee you do not keep is a Merchant Center misrepresentation. Empty = the line does not render.

settings.label: Customers line
settings.info: Ships empty on purpose — the old default ("Over 1,000+ happy customers") was a customer count no store had earned yet. Fill in your real figure, or leave it empty.

settings.content: Central on/off switches for every urgency, proof and helper element. Each element also hides when its text setting is emptied. The urgency switches ship OFF and stay off by default.

settings.label: Fit scale (PDP)
settings.info: Runs small / true to size / runs large marker, derived from custom.fit_note (override: custom.fit_scale). Renders nothing when no verdict can be derived.

settings.label: Newsletter popup
settings.info: Theme-owned newsletter popup (8s trigger, 30-day dismiss memory). ⚠️ Any discount promise in the popup copy REQUIRES a matching real discount in the store (fake-signal rule). Ships off by default: known issue where mobile lets you scroll it away — fix scroll-lock before re-enabling.

settings.label: Hide cart add-on lines
settings.info: The paid add-on (shipping protection) then appears ONLY as its toggle row, never as a cart line. Its price stays visible on the toggle and in the total.

settings.content: ⚠️ URGENCY + PROOF SWITCHES. These print claims about your store, so only turn one on once the claim is TRUE. The theme no longer generates any of these numbers — the pseudo-random scarcity tiers and the live-viewers line have been removed outright, and what remains prints exactly what you type in Storefront proof, or nothing.

settings.label: Stock line (PDP)
settings.info: Prints your Storefront-proof low-stock line on the product page. Inventory is untracked, so the same line shows on every product — only enable it if that statement is true across your catalogue.

settings.label: Star rating (PDP + cart) — ⚠️ needs a real source
settings.info: Prints the rating_value/rating_count you entered under Storefront proof. Keep OFF until a genuine review base backs those numbers — fabricated ratings breach consumer-protection law (DSA Art. 25, FTC).

settings.label: Cart drawer: express wallets
settings.info: Shows Shop Pay / Google Pay express buttons under the checkout button in the cart drawer. Off = calmer drawer, wallets still available in checkout.

settings.label: Enable bundle-discount bar
settings.info: Shows the tier bar in the cart drawer + cart page and the ladder on the PDP. ONLY enable after the matching Shopify automatic discounts are live — the bar is display-only and must mirror what checkout actually grants, or it is misrepresentation (GMC suspension risk).

settings.content: Your ToolSuite membership license. This is pre-filled when you download the theme from your ToolSuite dashboard. Manage it at toolsuite.com/dashboard/resources.

settings.label: License key
settings.info: Format: TS-…  — keep this filled to use the theme with your active ToolSuite membership.
